statusDetail: Completed atomic audit of the public unauthenticated login gateway. Authenticated Business Suite, Ads Manager, account recovery, and credentialed destinations were excluded because no test account was provided.

page.framework: Meta client runtime (no public framework marker)
page.notes: The requested URL redirects to a public login gateway. The gateway and consent state were audited; authenticated product templates were not silently treated as covered.

checkOutcomes.method: Default and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-emulated capture retained the same white modal and light page palette as the default capture.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated reduced motion plus getAnimations/computed transition probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched; no active animations or smooth scrolling were present, and the CSS inventory contained 32 reduced-motion rules.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and visual inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found “Allow all cookies” at 4.23:1 instead of the required 4.5:1.
The audited gateway has no same-document route swap; the loaded consent state is stable and no jarring animated swap was observed.
No scroll-linked animation or parallax was present, so native scrolling is not blocked by main-thread visual effects.
The gateway exposes ordinary buttons and document scrolling, with no custom swipe, drag, overscroll, or pointer-driven gesture that fights platform behavior.
No sticky or affixed application chrome is used on this compact gateway, so there is no static scroll chrome obscuring content.

checkOutcomes.method: Overlay/menu DOM and mobile screenshot inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The visible consent modal remains contained at 360px with zero horizontal overflow; no detached tooltip or manually drifting anchored surface was observed.
Purpose copy leads directly to four clearly named authentication choices, while the modal presents two explicit consent actions.
A modal consent wall obscures the core login page before user interaction.
The overlay uses role=dialog but has no accessible name and no aria-modal; the menu trigger also lacks an accessible label.
Behind the consent layer, the gateway is content-focused: one purpose block, four account actions, and a compact footer without a persistent app frame.
scrollWidth, clientWidth and innerWidth were all 360px; horizontalOverflowPx was 0 and viewport metadata was present.

checkOutcomes.method: CSSOM rule inventory and narrow screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSSOM probe found 31 container rules, and the consent surface reflowed from a wide desktop panel to a single-column 360px layout.
Twenty-eight actionable footer/locale links measured only 16px high.
The body states “Get started with business tools from Meta” and exposes Facebook, Instagram, account creation, and managed-account actions.
For the auditable public gateway, all four authentication handoff choices are present, named, focusable, and wired as actions; credentialed destinations were intentionally excluded.
The pre-authentication gateway contains no local data-entry or submit result state; credential errors and recovery occur beyond the unauthenticated scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public gateway has no local success/error/empty workflow to exercise.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse LCP was 11.6s and FCP 9.7s; the independent trace LCP was 3.25s.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout-shift observer and Lighthouse CLS
checkOutcomes.evidence: Both instruments reported CLS 0 with no observed shifts.
Trace found one 60.83ms long task and 10.83ms TBT; Lighthouse TBT was 32ms, both low.
112 requests transferred 2.14MB; 21 stylesheets included numerous parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority render-blocking candidates.
The gateway loaded 62 scripts (1.06MB) and 21 stylesheets (386KB) for a four-choice login surface.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits and DOM control probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed focusable links; the custom probe counted five unlabeled interactives.
The primary cookie acceptance control measured 4.23:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement.
No H1 and no semantic landmarks were found; all detected headings were H2 elements inside consent content.
Body copy wraps without clipping at 360px, remains readable, and the layout primitive found no overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Viewport metadata, reflow, and target-size probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: User scaling is not disabled and reflow has no overflow, but 28 links are only 16px high.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse console audit and failed-resource probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console passed, and the resource timing probe found no response status >=400.
HTML5 doctype, UTF-8 and viewport are present, but 8 of 9 images omit intrinsic dimensions and 8 use PNG.
The page produced no console errors, no failing timed resources, and no permission prompt on load; HTTPS passed.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata probe and Lighthouse SEO
checkOutcomes.evidence: A descriptive title exists, but meta description is absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO, link inventory, and viewport check
checkOutcomes.evidence: Robots and crawlable-anchor audits passed; real href links and viewport metadata are present.
The 200 public page has locale choices but no canonical or hreflang links.

checkOutcomes.method: Open Graph, Twitter Card and JSON-LD probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No Open Graph, Twitter Card or JSON-LD metadata was present.

checkOutcomes.method: Security headers, cookies, HTTPS and secret scan
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and CSP are present and no client secret was found, but Referrer-Policy is absent and CSP allows inline styles.

checkOutcomes.method: Cookie, tracker, and HAR-origin inspection before consent
checkOutcomes.evidence: Before a consent choice, CDP found zero cookies and no known tracker domains; external requests were confined to Meta-operated facebook.com/fbcdn.net origins.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load screenshot and authentication control inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: No browser permission prompt appeared; authentication offers Facebook, Instagram and a managed Meta account rather than exposing a local password form.
HSTS, DENY framing and Permissions-Policy are present, but Referrer-Policy is missing.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML versus rendered DOM discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Only 11% of rendered content words were available in raw HTML without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: Runtime, mobile layout and console inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The modal stays within a 360px viewport with zero horizontal overflow, no console errors, and no failing resource status observed.
The audited surface is an online authentication gateway to account-bound business services; offline task completion is not meaningful.
checkOutcomes.reason: An unauthenticated login gateway to intrinsically online account services does not have a meaningful offline core task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: When script execution is unavailable, only 11% of normal content survives and the primary rendered gateway is not preserved.
The document declares lang=en and exposes multiple clearly named locale choices; no forced LTR dir attribute conflicts with language selection.
The gateway displays no locale-sensitive date, number, currency, duration, address, or calendar data to format.
checkOutcomes.reason: No locale-sensitive data appears on the audited public gateway.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The gateway presents no times, events, schedules, or recurring intervals.
checkOutcomes.reason: No temporal data or scheduling feature appears on the audited public gateway.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load consent screenshots and control comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mandatory full-screen consent detour blocks all authentication actions before they can be used.
document.forms was empty and the public gateway exposes no local editable fields or validation state.
checkOutcomes.reason: No local form validation or error-feedback surface exists on this gateway.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The DOM contains no public input fields requiring autocomplete or input assistance.
checkOutcomes.reason: No editable inputs exist on the audited public gateway.

checkOutcomes.evidence: All account actions are blocked until the separate consent overlay is handled.

checkOutcomes.method: Image audit and HAR weight inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Eight legacy PNG images lack dimensions; responsive sources are missing on five and below-fold consent images load eagerly.
Initial load performs 112 requests including 62 scripts and fetches offscreen consent illustrations.
Meta CDN and related-origin traffic accounts for 101 requests and 2.08MB of 2.14MB transferred.
No WebMCP capabilities are exposed, but the public gateway has no safe domain action beyond handing off to credentialed authentication.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent capabilities would require authenticated, permissioned business context and are not appropriate on this unauthenticated gateway.

checkOutcomes.method: Built-in AI usage and feature-purpose assessment
checkOutcomes.evidence: The gateway performs no inference, summarisation, translation, or generative task.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no inference-relevant feature on the public login gateway.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap summaries around 10 repeated consent disclosure toggles
checkOutcomes.evidence: After repeated disclosure clicks, node count fell by 1,022 and retained self-size changed by only +38,219 bytes, with no Detached constructor in the top post-interaction list.
The baseline heap held 1,368,314 V8 nodes and 53.1MB self-size for a 716-element login gateway.
Node/edge counts decreased after repetition and no Detached constructor appeared in the post-interaction top constructors.

principleOutcomes.reason: Agent capabilities would require authenticated, permissioned business context and are not appropriate on this unauthenticated gateway. There is no inference-relevant feature on the public login gateway.

paths.description: Public pre-authentication gateway and initial cookie-consent state, representing the only accessible template. Audited at desktop, 360x800, dark preference, reduced motion, and no-JavaScript crawler conditions. Authenticated Business Suite, Ads Manager, credential recovery, and post-login workflows were not covered because they require credentials.

findings.summary: The public login and consent surfaces do not adapt to dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in palette and file size to the default capture: white modal and light page surfaces remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use preference-driven surface/text tokens, retaining tested contrast in both schemes.

findings.summary: The primary cookie acceptance control narrowly misses minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the 12px bold white “Allow all cookies” label at 4.23:1 against #1877f2, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the button foreground/background token to reach at least 4.5:1 and verify forced-colors behavior.

findings.summary: A blocking cookie interstitial obscures the core login content immediately on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show the consent dialog covering most of the first viewport before any user action; the underlying login actions are dimmed and unavailable.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface that limits blocking to what is legally necessary and preserves immediate access to essential context/actions.

findings.summary: The consent overlay lacks complete modal semantics.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found role=dialog but no accessible label and no aria-modal; the control inventory also found an unlabeled menu-style control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog or complete role=dialog semantics with aria-modal, an accessible name, focus containment, and deterministic focus return.

findings.summary: Many footer and locale links have undersized touch hit areas.
findings.evidence: The computed target probe found 28 interactive links only 16px high, including Privacy, Terms, language choices, and Help Centre.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing so touch targets are at least 24px minimum, preferably 44px on mobile, while retaining visible keyboard focus.

findings.summary: Cold-load paint performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 9.7s, LCP 11.6s, Speed Index 9.7s, and time to interactive 11.9s. A separate trace still measured LCP 3.25s, above the good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP content, reduce critical CSS/script dependencies, and verify under representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The login gateway has a long, heavy critical-resource path.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 112 requests and 2,140,487 transferred bytes, including 21 stylesheets and multiple parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority CSS candidates; 101 requests and 2.08MB came from related external origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse and prune critical CSS, preload only proven critical assets, defer nonessential consent illustrations and scripts, and apply durable caching.

findings.summary: The simple gateway ships disproportionate script and stylesheet volume.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 62 scripts transferring 1,057,506 bytes plus 21 stylesheets transferring 385,868 bytes for a page whose visible task is choosing one of four login methods.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage and bundle analysis to remove unused modules and route-split consent/help code and authenticated-product code from the gateway.

findings.summary: Focusable links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse link-name audit failed on two tab-order anchors, including a store link and the consent menu trigger; the custom probe counted five unlabeled interactive elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a stable accessible name and use native button/link semantics where possible.

findings.summary: The page lacks a useful top-level heading and landmark structure.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contained no H1 and no main, nav, header, footer, aside, or equivalent role landmarks; only consent-content H2 elements were detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single descriptive H1 and semantic main/nav/footer landmarks, then verify focus enters and exits the modal predictably.

findings.summary: Interactive footer and language targets are too short for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The target-size probe measured 28 actionable links at 16px high. Mobile reflow itself had no horizontal overflow, so the failure is target sizing rather than layout width.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand clickable padding without preventing zoom and retest at 200% zoom and 360px reflow.

findings.summary: Most consent illustrations omit intrinsic dimensions and use legacy PNG delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 8 of 9 images without width/height, 8 PNG assets, 5 without responsive sources, and 2 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load below-fold illustrations, and serve appropriately sized AVIF/WebP responsive sources.

findings.summary: The public gateway has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe and Lighthouse agree that the title exists but meta[name=description] is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique description explaining that this page signs users into Meta business tools.

findings.summary: Localized login URLs have no canonical or hreflang signals.
findings.evidence: Metadata inspection found no canonical link, no alternate hreflang links, and no robots meta despite a visible locale selector.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a stable canonical and reciprocal hreflang alternates for indexable locale variants, aligned with sitemap and robots policy.

findings.summary: The public organization/login page has no share-preview or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: Metadata inspection found no Open Graph tags, Twitter card tags, or JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and minimal Open Graph metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: The response omits Referrer-Policy and permits inline styles in CSP.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY and Permissions-Policy, but no Referrer-Policy; CSP style-src includes unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy and continue reducing CSP unsafe-inline usage with hashes/nonces where feasible.

findings.summary: Most meaningful gateway content is unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 11% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML: 37 raw content tokens versus 185 rendered, with crawler and rendered screenshots materially different.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the purpose, login choices, and essential consent text/actions; hydrate only interaction enhancements.

findings.summary: The JavaScript-disabled/network-degraded state loses most of the primary experience.
findings.evidence: The no-JavaScript crawler capture retained only 11% of rendered content, demonstrating that a failed script delivery removes the normal login gateway rather than presenting a useful fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide server-rendered fallback login links and an actionable retry/status message when required client resources fail.

findings.summary: Consent blocks the account task before the user can proceed.
findings.evidence: On both desktop and mobile the consent wall appears first and disables the underlying sign-in choices; mobile dedicates nearly the full viewport to the prompt. Decline and allow controls are visually similar, but the interruption remains coercive by placement.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the blocking surface, make essential use possible without optional consent, and keep decline/revisit controls as direct and durable as acceptance.

findings.summary: The authentication entry is gated behind a separate full-screen consent decision.
findings.evidence: The first-load screenshots show all four account actions dimmed beneath the consent overlay, adding a mandatory detour before authentication.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep privacy choice clear but decouple optional-cookie consent from access to essential authentication wherever policy permits.

findings.summary: Consent artwork is delivered inefficiently.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 8 legacy PNGs, 8 images without dimensions, 5 without responsive sources, and two below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert decorative illustrations to modern formats, add responsive sources/intrinsic sizes, and defer assets outside the visible consent panel.

findings.summary: The gateway performs substantial work unrelated to its visible task.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 112 requests, 62 scripts and 21 stylesheets; several offscreen consent-card images are fetched on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer hidden consent detail assets and noncritical modules until requested, and deprioritise background work.

findings.summary: Related-origin CDN traffic dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: 101 of 112 requests and 2,079,503 of 2,140,487 transferred bytes came from static.xx.fbcdn.net or www.facebook.com. Even treating these as Meta-operated infrastructure, the transfer is disproportionate for a login chooser.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict route budget, remove nonessential dependencies, and defer media/help assets until opened.

findings.summary: The baseline JavaScript heap is large for a pre-authentication gateway.
findings.evidence: Heap summary reported 1,368,314 V8 nodes, 4,244,945 edges and 53,144,077 self-size bytes while the rendered DOM contained only 716 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained native/object populations and avoid loading authenticated-product runtime and hidden consent content before it is needed.

taskList.title: Make the primary gateway server-rendered and resilient
Cut the login route critical path and bundle budget
Replace the blocking consent experience with an accessible, proportionate flow
Restore semantic structure, names, contrast, and target sizing
Add preference-driven dark styling and tighten response policies
